launches.title: UpCodes - Copilot for building codes
launches.tagline: AI-powered building code research assistant
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** UpCodes Copilot accelerates building code research for anyone involved in the compliance process for design and construction by providing tailored responses and relevant regulations to project-specific questions.

# **Managing compliance is difficult**

In today’s complex regulatory environment, compliance management is critical in ensuring safety in our built environments. However, as these codes become more comprehensive, they become more challenging to manage and meet. Homeowners, developers, architects, engineers, builders, and government officials spend significant amounts of time dissecting and working with the code. 

The code ecosystem is not only incredibly dense but also constantly changing. We host over 5 million code sections and 1,700+ state and city codes, [update over 7,000 sections per month (on average)](https://up.codes/code-accuracy), and host over 160,000 local amendments. Other challenges include the difficulty of working across multiple jurisdictions and maintaining firm-wide code expertise. 

# **Current AI tools are limited**

Generic AI chatbots (like ChatGPT, Google Bard, Bing Chat, etc.) work from out-of-date code and is not jurisdiction-specific. Because the codes change dramatically across adoption cycles and jurisdictions, for many codes, UpCodes is often the only place that is continually integrating local amendments or changes to the code.

# **Introducing UpCodes Copilot**

At UpCodes, we envision a world where architects, engineers, contractors, and everyone involved in the building compliance lifecycle can work together seamlessly and harness the power of AI to create safer buildings. We’re in the early innings of that future, and it’s why we’re excited to announce UpCodes Copilot. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=72667&key=user_uploads/147166/5481c27f-f364-4ce9-9449-de817a1bf363)

Our vision is that Copilot becomes an indispensable research assistant for designers, builders, plan reviewers, and plan examiners. Instead of manually parsing through dense code sections, Copilot accelerates code research process by instantly delivering tailored responses to any code query. With Copilot you can: 

* **Research faster** – Go beyond manually gathering code sections from various codes and chapters. 
* **Be more efficient** – Catch sections you may have missed and better manage compliance. 
* **Gain insight** – Unlock the ability to parse through massive quantities of code.

# **Who Copilot is for**

UpCodes Copilot is for anyone involved in the code compliance lifecycle. Most architects, engineers, and general contractors already know how cumbersome and difficult it is to gather context and gain insight into what the code is saying. Wherever someone is in the architectural design process, whether they’re designing, building, or managing occupancy, Copilot will accelerate their understanding of the code.

# **How Copilot works**

Copilot builds on our powerful search that surfaces relevant content across our 5+ million code sections by directly answering tough code questions. Its responses are based on analysis across multiple code sections (including tables and charts!) as well as basic calculations. And best yet, Copilot always cites the sections it pulls from so anyone can validate the response and deepen their code expertise.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=72667&key=user_uploads/147166/1e0ce9d8-73f1-4e6b-9527-6641b8b15322)

([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=695G3xNKk_o))

# **What you can use Copilot for**

* **Ask a code question** – Ask code questions for a specific jurisdiction and adoption cycle and get answers that point out the relevant code sections.\
  Example: “I have a parking lot with 200 spaces. How many van-accessible spaces do I need?”
* **Explain a concept or code section** – Get detailed explanations for complex concepts or specific code sections. \
  Example: “Can you explain what 'fire separation distance' means in the context of building code?"‍
* **Find related sections** – Identify code sections that correspond to a specific topic you’re researching. \
  Example: "Find all sections related to plumbing codes in a residential building."
* **Perform a calculation** – Provide your project parameters to Copilot and let it calculate the code requirements for you. \
  Example: “Help me determine the maximum occupancy of a building, given its size…”‍
* **Summarize what the code is saying** – For lengthy code sections, ask Copilot to give you an overview of the key points.\
  Example: "Summarize the key points from Section 101.2 of CBC 2022."‍
* **Generate a checklist for a focus area** – Get a tailored checklist for that specific focus area to help you ensure all requirements are met. \
  Example: “Provide a checklist for designing a Type 1 grease duct for a fryer in a commercial kitchen. The kitchen is on the ground floor of a 3-story building. Ventilation equipment will be placed on the roof.”

# **Ask**

* If you would like to try Copilot, sign up for an [UpCodes trial](https://upcodes.ai) to test it out for free! 
* If you know of any architecture, engineering, or general contracting firms, we would love to chat! You can reach us at [sales@up.codes](mailto:sales@up.codes).

launches.tagline: Downtobid gives construction estimators an AI-assistant to make bidding faster.
launches.body:
# **TLDR**

[Downtobid](https://downtobid.com/) is building AI to understand construction blueprints. Our first product is a modern bidding tool equipped with an AI assistant to make bidding faster.

# **The Problem**

Construction blueprints are very difficult to read and understand, which makes bidding slow and expensive for construction teams. Bidding is the process of getting a set of blueprints and reaching out to subcontractors to get prices on each scope of work (e.g., drywall, electrical, mechanical), then compiling these quotes into a single estimated price for the project.

For example, here's a 474-page PDF for a new wellness center (a medium size project). A general contractor needs to understand all the intricate details of this project in order to price it effectively.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/3c08be04-5f62-45ee-aaa4-dae24483c74c)

Every page contains a lot of information about materials that need to be purchased (e.g., which walls should be added, and specifications for the lighting system).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/6903f0a7-6817-4aef-b5bd-67f30b53f6c6)

# **The Solution**

Downtobid is an all-in-one bidding tool equipped with an AI assistant that streamlines every part of the bidding process for general contractors, from understanding the construction plans to reaching out to vendors.

### _AI to find scope of work_

Today, GCs spend 2-3 hours per project reading large construction documents to figure out what vendors they need to get quotes from. With Downtobid, GCs simply upload a set of plans and AI instantly calls out which scopes of work are required and highlights them on the actual set of plans. Rather than read blueprints raw, GCs get an annotated version with all important info called out.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/9723f21b-081c-4a34-b838-52c113f8c81f)

### _AI to build project-specific subcontractor lists_

Today, GCs need to build custom subcontractor lists based on their project requirements. Not every subcontractor is a good fit for the project (e.g. you wouldn't invite a wood-flooring sub to a building that requires carpet flooring). With Downtobid, AI auto-recommends a list of subs based on their expertise, experience, and project requirements.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/13887d59-73f9-468a-a671-6ab3d3e2a924)

_AI orchestrates the outreach process_

Today, GCs have to send emails, set up Dropbox links (to host their plans), and send follow-up emails. With Downtobid, AI prepares your email campaign and automatically follows up with subcontractors when they don't respond. A GC simply needs to respond to emails in their inbox and wait for proposals to come back.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/44db1129-ebe1-42de-b495-5a7ca8def8cd)

**Long-term vision**

Our long-term plan is to create intelligent AI that can understand and interpret construction blueprints. We started with bidding has the lowest requirements for AI so it's the quickest way to market. As the AI for construction gets more intelligent, we'll be able to handle more and more construction workflows. For example, we’re starting to annotate plans so LLMs can better understand the structure of construction blueprints.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/b4e77874-f0f2-4ee4-b1c9-7acbf773c545)

**Team**

We spent the last 5 years working together on another bidding product (for subs) called BasisBoard. Previously, Andy worked at Uber on self-driving cars, and Kev worked at Boston Consulting Group as a designer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=80238&key=user_uploads/252451/5d7e3304-3d0f-4945-9318-4e0eb226af45)

**Ask**

We'd love intros to general contractors, especially those who are building retail projects (e.g., Walmart, Lululemon, Dior, McDonald's, etc.). You can even direct them to our [website](https://downtobid.com/) to try our AI on a set of their construction plans for free.

launches.title: Handoff H1: a takeoff model that outperforms human estimators
launches.tagline: Autonomous takeoffs, available today via API
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** H1 reads construction blueprints and produces a complete material takeoff autonomously, from the raw PDF. It scores 81.6% on our benchmark — ahead of human estimators (77.6%) and \~20 points clear of the best frontier model. It runs in \~2 hours vs. up to a week for a human.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106241&key=user_uploads/428748/ccaeb6b3-ba3f-4330-acd0-8e8ff779cca2)


**The problem**

Before a contractor can bid a job, someone has to do a takeoff: read every sheet, count materials trade by trade, measure walls and roofs, cross-reference dimensions that live on different pages. It takes an experienced estimator 8–20 hours per project and years of training to do at all. It's the tax on every bid in a huge, fragmented industry.

You'd think a frontier model could do this now. It can't. Foundation models today aren't capable of understanding construction drawings to a level that is actually useful for a construction business. So this massive $2 trillion industry still runs on blueprints that are being analyzed by humans pretty much the same way they have been for the last few hundred years.

**What we built**

Handoff has developed H1: an AI model that understands and analyzes blueprints better than a human estimator, thus resolving this manual bottleneck once and for all.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106241&key=user_uploads/428748/e3a9fd8f-cdf2-48f1-b4d6-9e30aa807ec5)

H1 has three layers:

* **Scope analysis** — a detailed, trade-by-trade breakdown of what the project actually involves, read straight from the drawings.
* **Takeoff with quantities** — a complete material quantity list per trade: framing members, sheets, linear and square footage, counts, all with units.
* **Localized construction costs** — accurate pricing on those quantities, localized to your ZIP code.

All of it programmatic and autonomous. No human needs to be involved in the process of creating the entire takeoff. You can simply upload plans and get structured scope, quantities, and costed output back.

**The benchmark (TakeoffBench-V1)**

As part of this, we are also releasing the industry's first takeoff benchmark that enables us and anybody else in the research community to compare models against 15 real, permissioned, PII-stripped residential blueprint sets, each paired with a consensus-validated expert takeoff.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106241&key=user_uploads/428748/b4f0b802-c841-403e-8867-5b1ac2e9fcb2)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106241&key=user_uploads/428748/abdfeb2b-4ed7-4764-bc47-a6305f6d8ff9)

Here's how we performed on the benchmark:

* Handoff-H1: 81.6%
* human estimator (with takeoff software): 77.6%
* best frontier model (Claude Fable): 61.4%

The rest cluster in the low-to-mid 50s (gpt-5.6, Claude, Kimi) down to 34.7% (DeepSeek-V4-Pro).

launches.body:
**TL;DR: 1build is launching the API for construction pricing data. Developers can use our API to access up-to-date information on construction costs for workflows like construction estimating, procurement, and loan/insurance underwriting. The API can be either queried with GraphQL or easily integrated into any application with one line of HTML.**

﻿📚﻿ **Backstory**

As wild as it sounds, the construction industry still uses actual books that are published once a year to track construction market pricing. I previously ran the data science team at CloudKitchens where I needed an API for tracking live construction pricing data--but instead of an API I had to deal with these cost books.

![](https://t4207102.p.clickup-attachments.com/t4207102/24e83b10-e8f3-4b04-b043-a050c01c2eb1/image.png)

﻿📊﻿ **Problem**

Construction costs have been extremely volatile over the last several years. For example, lumber prices skyrocketed 400% and then crashed in 2021. At the same time, the construction tech space is booming ($5B+ is invested annually), but it still lacks its own "Plaid" for mission-critical market pricing data.

﻿🛠️﻿ **Our solution**

1build has an easy-to-use API as well as a JavaScript embed widget that gives you access to live pricing data on 68 million construction materials, labor, and equipment anywhere in the US.

﻿🚀﻿ **How it works**

You can either use our GraphQL API ([docs](https://developer.1build.com/1build-api-reference)) or JavaScript embed widget ([docs](https://developer.1build.com/1build-widget-reference/)) to integrate construction pricing data into your application. Sign up [here](https://app2.1build.com/public/register?signupType=SOFTWARE_DEVELOPER) to get your API key.

Here are just some of the use cases for our data:

* Your contractor sent you an estimate and you want to validate their quote vs market rates.
* You're serving bank underwriters who need to check whether their client's construction loan application has an accurate budget.
* You're working with insurance brokers who need to approve a quote for home repairs.

﻿👷 ﻿**Asks**

launches.body:
I’m excited to announce our newest product - [**Clad Locates**](https://www.withclad.com/locates/overview)

**Clad Locates is an AI-assisted tool that helps contractors create and manage utility locate requests (811 tickets).** 

We’re live in Alabama right now, and will expand to more states soon.

### The Problem

Contractors dig all the time - to place internet cables, upgrade pipes, build fences, and more. 

Before a contractor can begin excavating, they are required to call in a utility locate request. This is to make sure the contractor digs safely - that they won’t hit a gas pipe, for example.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93588&key=user_uploads/448610/eb053624-67ff-4b07-8abf-d10ece228cb4)

For contractors, handling these tickets is critically important, but a pain:

1. Submitting tickets takes a lot of time and distracts project managers from higher value work.
2. Making sure tickets don’t expire is also necessary, so contractors avoid a ‘down day’ (a day where they can’t work, due to an expired 811 request). 

With 43M tickets submitted last year by tens of thousands of contractors, this is not a small problem.

So we decided to fix it.

### We’ve made handling locates a breeze for contractors

https://youtu.be/Y04NyOXGt2o

We built Clad Locates to make it fast and easy to submit and track 811 tickets.

1. **AI-driven narratives -** We use AI to eliminate the most time consuming part of submitting a ticket, writing a ‘narrative,’ (to describe the path that a contractor will excavate.
2. **Bulk Submission -** Clad connects with the state 811 systems to submit tickets automatically, 1 ticket at a time or 15 all at once.
3. **Automated Tracking -** We get data from the state 811 systems to build an automated automated tracker to monitor when areas are ready to dig, and when tickets will be expiring.
4. **Expiration Notifications** - To prevent ‘down days,’ Clad notifies contractors when tickets are expiring and need to be renewed. Soon, contractors will be able to renew tickets directly from Clad. 

### Join our waitlist and reach out!

Reach out to us at jason@withclad.com, or sign up on our [website](https://www.withclad.com/locates/overview) to learn more.

launches.title: sizeless - Spatial AI for underground infrastructure 🚧
launches.tagline: Turn a 10-minute phone video of an open trench into engineering-grade documentation
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're Julius, Cornelius and Roger — the founders of sizeless.

**TL;DR**

sizeless turns a smartphone video of an open trench into the documentation utilities and contractors are legally required to produce: a 3D model, CAD/BIM plans, and the quantities they bill from. Today that takes months and a surveyor. We do it in hours, from a video the crew films themselves.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=114663&key=user_uploads/1260577/02c85a25-fa1a-43a2-ad56-6e571b257b37)

### **Problem ❌**

Everything under a street — gas, water, power, heat, fiber — must be documented when it is built or repaired. That documentation is still done by hand: schedule a surveyor, drive out, measure with a tape or a GPS rover, write it on paper, go back to the office and draw it. Then the next contractor does the same thing again, for their own pipe, in the same trench.

Our average customer **waits 6 months** for documentation and spends around **$4M a year per German city** on it.

And once the trench is backfilled, nobody can check whether the numbers were right. One person's reading, one moment, unrepeatable. That is why crews keep hitting lines that "aren't there".

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=114663&key=user_uploads/1260577/f446f4ae-943d-4c83-ba7e-c48b9220eca7)

### **Solution ✅**

The crew films the open trench with a phone for about 10 minutes. Then:

**Our SLAM engine** builds a metric 3D model from that video — no surveyor, no scanner, and it works without GPS in basements and house connections

**Our vision engine** recognises the components — pipe types, diameters, fittings, couplings — and attributes them

**Our agent** produces what the customer actually files: CAD/BIM, GIS, quantities, and invoice-ready numbers

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=114663&key=user_uploads/1260577/bbaddb8c-abbf-43ad-8866-025cde7bb93b)

The crew also talks while filming, and that goes into the record:

> _"There was a gas pipe crossing, so we had to lay this pipe approximately\
> 50 cm below it."_

No point cloud and no plan ever captures the _reason_ for a deviation — and once the trench is closed, it is gone for good. That sentence, anchored to the exact position in 3D, is the part nobody else has.

**Where we are:** seven paid pilots in three months, the first converted to an annual contract, working with utilities and contractors on district heating in Germany.

**Why now:** phones do metric 3D capture, reconstruction got cheap, and vision-language models read attributes rather than just detecting boxes. And the long game: construction robots are coming, and nobody holds the training data for what is underground. That is the layer we are building.

### **Ask 💬**

**Intros to utilities, municipal works, or civil and pipeline contractors** - Europe or the US

**Anyone who has sold into municipalities or utilities:** how did you shorten those cycles?

**Founders in construction tech, geospatial or robotics** — would love to compare notes

If you know someone running a **family construction business**, that is often our fastest door in

You can reach us at [julius@sizeless.co](mailto:julius@sizeless.co) (commercial) or [cornelius@sizeless.co](mailto:cornelius@sizeless.co) (technical).

### **Team**

**Julius** (CEO) — ex-Chief of Staff to the CEO at Aon.

**Cornelius** (CTO) — PhD in robotics and computer vision at ETH Zürich's Autonomous Systems Lab. Built perception systems for railways, and a wearable navigation system for blind users.

**Roger** (Science lead) — professor of physics & AI. Spent a decade recovering 3D structure from sparse, noisy measurements; in his case, mapping the universe.

_Fun fact: the hardest part of our capture pipeline is not the maths, it is that trenches are wet, muddy, and full of moving excavators — which breaks every off-the-shelf 3D reconstruction method we tried._

launches.body:
### **Tl;dr**

[Line](https://www.line.build/?utm_source=YCLaunch&utm_medium=post) empowers contractors with tools that make building decarbonization projects affordable for their customers and boosts conversion rates. We consolidate the thousands of rebates, incentives, and green financing options for energy efficiency upgrades, and make it easy for contractors to secure funding for their customers.

**We’re looking for intros to HVAC installers and electrification services for our pilot**. And if you’re thinking about getting a heat pump, we’d love to help you find and apply for rebates and other incentives. Get in touch at [founders@line.build](mailto:founders@line.build)

### **The Problem**

With buildings accounting for almost 40% of US GHG emissions, retrofitting for efficiency is essential to reduce emissions and load on the grid, but expensive. Over $80B of rebates, incentives and financing is available but hyper-fragmented across utilities, federal funds, grants, and green lending programs. Contractors are often responsible for helping consumers navigate this fragmented landscape - not only does their consumer demand it, but many sources of funding require it. This is leading to an increase in overhead, as they hire Ops teams and consultants to meet demand. Contractors that do not provide this service are seeing their conversion impacted, as consumers look to maximize savings. 

### **Our Solution**

Line is a single source of truth for all available funding options. By providing a few pieces of information, such as project address and scope, contractors can easily access all available incentives and financing options available to their customer. Requirements are consolidated and distilled in a simple manner and we make suggestions that help contractors maximize savings for their customers. Maximized savings, means maximized conversion!

Once the customer is ready to proceed with the project, the contractor can leverage a common application to apply for all eligible programs. We remove the hassle of navigating multiple websites, printing documents, or mailing applications.

Our platform is designed to be user-friendly, available in multiple languages, and accessible on both web and mobile devices. Additionally, we provide an API that seamlessly integrates with existing quoting tools, enhancing efficiency and convenience.

**_Tl;dr:_** _Constructable aggregates documents and communication from multiple sources so construction teams can answer questions quickly and accurately about their projects, saving them critical time and preventing costly mistakes._

Hi everyone,

We are [John](https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-yoder-92595985/), [Molly](https://www.linkedin.com/in/molly-abbott-41b03037/), and [Emma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/emmamedjuck/), former proptech product and engineering leaders and the team behind [Constructable](https://www.constructable.app/). We’re on a mission to give everyone on a construction project the information they need at their fingertips to deliver a project safely, accurately, and efficiently.

## **🧨 The Problem**

**Construction teams are spending too much time digging through data spread out in many places**

Construction projects are complex and constant change means a single project will have a huge amount of documentation. Take the San Francisco team we’re working with that just finished a major 3-year project. By the end of the project, they had a 2000-page plan that had changed hundreds of times, 2300 change orders, and thousands of bids, RFIs, and submittals going back and forth between the general contractor, developer, architect, engineers, and 93 specialty contractors. The team spent hours each week trying to find information across email, Procore, chat conversations, and document management systems.

Look at all the folders one of our customers has for just 1 project!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=73724&key=user_uploads/1393936/d805b330-519c-4775-a2c5-c6699a58a99c)

**Not finding accurate information quickly can be detrimental to a project**

Many teams waste time and hire additional people to sort through data and search for the answers they need, yet still mistakenly use outdated or incorrect information. A [**study**](https://www.constructiondive.com/news/contractors-lost-18-trillion-globally-in-2020-due-to-bad-data-new-report/606939/) by FMI found that “bad data” – including data that is inaccessible, inconsistent, or untimely  – **cost the global construction industry $1.85 trillion** in 2020. Operating off of outdated plans or missing information can lead to costly delays, expensive re-work, and in the worst cases can cause dangerous conditions for the crews on the ground.

## **✨ Our Solution**

Constructable is the central place to find any information and get questions answered about a construction project. We aggregate documents and communication from file management systems like OneDrive and Dropbox, construction management software like Procore and Autodesk, email, and chat apps and make it quick for teams to answer any question and find the relevant documentation.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=73724&key=user_uploads/1393936/9318d182-f037-4d41-a7cd-f6f4a7a90581)

Constructable makes it easy to:

* Compare bids from multiple specialty contractors and see if they are missing key components in their bid
* Find the most recent steel plan and highlight what has changed since the last revision
* See RFIs that have been outstanding for more than 2 weeks and the contact information of the requestee
* Find the change order that involved adding an additional wall to the lobby, link to the before and after plans, and list the difference in takeoffs because of the change
* Get the schedule of all specialty contractors working the following week and which supplies are still on backorder for each contractor
* Get data from the appliance manuals needed for maintenance teams once the project is delivered

## **The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=73724&key=user_uploads/1393936/05c0d913-f492-43de-babd-97f415d5c860)

We spent the past 10 years working together at Appfolio (Nasdaq: APPF), where Emma was a VP of Product, John was a VP of Engineering, and Molly was a product growth leader. We loved supporting the businesses that provide millions of people with exceptional living and workplace experiences and we’re excited to bring our experience to empower today’s builders to construct tomorrow’s communities.

Molly has first-hand experience in the world of construction. Her dad, husband, and brother-in-law are general contractors and specialty contractors and she previously worked for a large specialty contractor. She’s experienced the chaotic highs and lows that go into completing a large project, which has fueled her passion to bring new technology to the industry.

Connect us to general contractors, owner’s reps, large specialty contractors, or developers. We’d love to get their feedback! Pass along our [website](https://www.constructable.ai) or send us an email, [founders@constructable.app](https://mailto:founders@constructable.ai). We appreciate the support!

launches.body:
**TL;DR** 👋

Feldy is field-first AI for home service companies. It unifies jobsite capture, 3D building scans, estimates, and field documentation in one simple app.

We’ve grown to over 200 paying customers on the web over the last few months, and are now launching the mobile app so field teams can use the full product on site.

Zayne and Shelby are construction software veterans with a combined 10+ years building computer vision and spatial AI tools.

**Meet Feldy:**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W0lEF7isKg4>

**The Problem:**

The biggest problem in residential home services in 2026 is still remarkably simple: estimates do not go out fast enough to homeowners.

An estimate is the quote a homeowner receives explaining what work will be done and how much it will cost. Yet, if you call a window contractor, or painter, it can still take two or three days, often longer, to receive one. Over the last 8 months, my home became a test bed for remodeling projects, and this is one of the few truths that persisted. This problem appears in nearly every trade we encountered.

_So why so long?_

The surprising part is that many of these estimates are not inherently complicated.

Consider a typical window and door contractor. A sales representative drives to the property, walks through the home, identifies every window and door, photographs existing conditions, and asks discovery questions:

* Do you want to replace the trim?
* Should the opening change?

Capturing this information can easily consume most of a one- or two-hour appointment. By the time the rep understands the property and records everything the office needs, there is _very little time left_ to actually sell the project. This is the primary reason quotes arrive days later, or require a second visit.

Furthermore, existing software makes the problem worse.

Most contractor tools have always been structured like digital forms. The software records what the estimator has already figured out, but it does very little to help figure out the job.

This is what led us to ask: what does this contractor world look like if the software recorded and figured out the job at once? Well, that’s Feldy.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110395&key=user_uploads/1494934/6bdd00aa-4517-41c6-897e-517110044d2b)

**So how do we solve this?**

Instead of requiring the person in the field to manually observe and organize everything, Feldy uses in-house computer vision and vision-language models to perform much of this _low-value work_: necessary technical work that consumes the majority of the job visit time, but creates little visible value for the homeowner.

The contractor _captures_ the property via photos/videos, lidar scans, or job walkthroughs (video and audio are combined). Feldy then interprets the capture and helps turn it into an estimate amongst a host of other workflow items such as inspection reports, proposals, materials lists, etc.

The entire thesis behind Feldy can be summed up as:

_How do we remove the time-consuming thinking required from the estimator that creates little visible value for the homeowner?_

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110395&key=user_uploads/1494934/060ca1ad-5038-40a5-868f-fb14eb04b164)

**The Scale of the bottleneck**

Angi’s list has estimated that American households undertake more than 700 million home projects annually.

Using 600 million estimates (aggressive case):

* 600M estimates \* 3.5 hours = 2.1 billion total labor hours
* 50% spent on measuring, documenting, takeoff, and estimate construction = 1.05 billion hours
* At $45–50 fully loaded cost = $47–53 billion in annual labor capacity tied up in that work

If Feldy reclaims 1–1.25 hours per estimate:

* 750 million hours returned
* Roughly $27–37 billion in productive capacity per year.

For the average home-services company, this is equivalent to reclaiming $50,000–$100,000+ in capacity each year, capacity that can be converted directly into more estimates, lower overhead, and higher revenue.

**The Team**

Zayne and Shelby met at UC Berkeley’s engineering school nearly 10 years ago. For the last three years, they have worked side by side building technology for the construction and home-services industries.

Together, they previously took a construction-software company from zero to $500k ARR in months. 

The pair is more excited than ever to build the next generation of software for home-service businesses.

**The ask**

If you know anyone who works in home services, tell them about Feldy and ask them to download the app!

Search Feldy AI on [IOS ](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/feldy-ai/id6780327228)and [Android ](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.feldy.app)app stores.

**TL;DR**

[Aether](https://aetherenergie.com/) offers an AI-powered end-to-end platform for rooftop solar installers. We combine advancements in computer vision/lidar and LLMs to bring a unique workflow automation tool for solar installers worldwide.

## Before we start, a sneak peek at Aether:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79053&key=user_uploads/1527633/4dd1fd38-1a6f-42f1-b8b8-1ad5d62ea174)

## Some Background

---

Hey all, we’re [Shelby Bons](https://linkedin.com/in/shelby-bons-ucberkeley) and [Zayne Sagar](https://linkedin.com/in/zaynesager), two climate entrepreneurs! Our fundamental mission is to make rooftop solar energy accessible and cheap throughout the world.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79053&key=user_uploads/1527633/561a67f7-4f40-419e-af7f-2ff7557ac5b7)

For rooftop solar to be deployed, it’s really up to solar installers. To us, the people who run these companies are our heroes. Last year we spoke to hundreds of solar installers and one thing is clear - they don’t have the tools to make them successful. We reimagined rooftop solar software from the ground up for them.

Aether _automates the boring stuff for solar installers using AI_.

## **❌** The Problem:

The biggest problem in US rooftop solar is still solar soft costs. These are non-hardware costs associated with a solar project, and they amount to north of 60% of the total solar cost of an installed system! If you reduce this you create more demand for rooftop solar in the market = better outcome for our planet.

**Contributors to high soft costs:**

* **PV CAD Design teams still manually build rooftop PV site designs**. This is time-consuming and prone to lots of errors. Mistakes here mean re-doing plansets and permitting which can cost $1k - $2k extra.
* **Almost all solar design tools are inaccurate in production and consumption modeling**. This is what tells rooftop owners “Is this the right investment for me?” Most solar tools were built as a sidekick for sales reps, with just enough basic estimates to sell a solar proposal. Consumers are smarter now and recent legal litigations are forcing better modeling to be done when selling solar.
* **Dependency on multiple platforms:** Most solar companies use a software stack of 6 - 10 point solutions. Collectively the solution is dumb and creates chaotic workflows where deals get lost and project delays happen a lot. This is very expensive.
* **Lack of project visibility across teams** causing lost sales deals, and project delays

We estimate $5k to $ 7k added soft costs for a typical rooftop project occurring because of the above.

## **✅** Solution:

**Aether is built to streamline the rooftop solar workflow end to end. Think Procore or Veeva but for Solar with an AI twist.**

With Aether, solar companies can rapidly generate PV site designs, sell using a beautiful PV proposal, and then manage it to installation in one simplified workflow.

Aether is made up of hubs that help specific roles in a solar installation company do their job, but more importantly, collaborate with other teams as needed with the help of AI.

**Our two core innovations:**

* We built an in-house computer vision model.
* We also decided to build a mini fine-tuned model for solar. Being trained on items such as system production data, vision model outputs, etc. (Can’t give the rest of our sauce away!)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79053&key=user_uploads/1527633/a0dc44ab-bc4f-498d-bc2d-7318a4751d70)

**The result is a unified AI platform to streamline solar with solar agents.**

[Aether Platform - Sneak Peak](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EFJuKOI8kEs&feature=youtu.be)

**💲Opportunity:** Aether will be a big player in the young and emerging Solar software vertical, which has a projected 20B Global TAM up for grabs by 2025.

## About Us

_Shelby and Zayne met at UC Berkeley close to a decade ago both originally being born in complete opposite ends of the world, France and Fiji._

_Shelby studied Materials Science and Engineering at UC Berkeley and was briefly headed for a Ph.D. in Theoretical Physics before founding Aether. She has worked at Dolby Laboratories, Voltaiq, and Sunrun in Data Science & Machine Learning roles._

_Zayne had brief stints at multiple climate-driven companies, working on problems around space-based weather data and energy modeling problems at the intersection of software. He has built high-performing product & engineering teams from the ground up by the age of 28._

launches.tagline: Engineers designing everything from cars to skyscrapers use our software to turn 3D models into the detailed 2D fabrication drawings that manufacturers require.
launches.body:
# TLDR

Mechanical engineers and designers dedicate around 40% of their time to the labor-intensive process of converting 3D models into 2D fabrication drawings, crucial for manufacturers. Using [**DraftAid**](https://draftaid.io/), teams can automate this process with a single click and:

* Save considerable time
* Direct their focus toward more value-added tasks
* Cut down on drawing errors, preventing expensive manufacturing mistakes

# **The problem**

Modern design teams initiate their design by 3D modeling. To get their design manufactured, they need to make 2D drawings that look something like this:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=78878&key=user_uploads/89898/590e3017-c1e8-4987-a30a-2c8469a2a8d6)

Making 2D drawings for what’s already been modeled in 3D takes up considerable time and energy. Design teams find themselves stuck investing 40% of their time in this manual task. This causes project delays while keeping talented designers busy doing repetitive tasks.

Like any other repetitive manual task, making drawings can also be quite error-prone. Even with accurate designs, errors often sneak in and are only found when fixing them is an expensive endeavor.

# **Enter DraftAid:**

Our innovation streamlines the drafting process making it as effortless as a single click. Once engineers complete their 3D design, a single click swiftly produces a manufacturing-ready 2D drawing within seconds.

The resulting drawing is entirely editable, allowing engineers to make any necessary adjustments before sending it off for manufacturing.

DraftAid allows teams to slash their current drawing time by up to 90% and eliminate common drawing errors. This not only enhances efficiency but also ensures consistency in drawings throughout the company, improving overall readability.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=78878&key=user_uploads/290663/9f289b2c-ea8a-4f13-9a4e-f317ac9cd804)

# **Meet the Power Trio:**

We are Mohammed, Abdullah, and Tahsin, a formidable team with a bond forged over three dynamic years of collaboration.

Before the inception of DraftAid, [**Mohammed Al-arnawoot**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammed-al-arnawoot/)’s journey included roles as a software engineer and later as a VP of engineering (@ Emagin, acquired by Innovyze) and a Director (@ Dozr) in several start-ups. Navigating the challenging terrain from pre-seed to Series X.

[**Abdullah Elqabbany**](https://linkedin.com/in/abdullah-elqabbany-8160551a8) is an electro-mechanical engineer who boasts a career marked by the creation of tens of thousands of drawings. Frustrated by the absence of a suitable drawing automation tool in his last role, he took matters into his own hands and built one from scratch.

[**Tahsin Rahman**](https://linkedin.com/in/muhammed-tahsin-rahman) is a distinguished PhD graduate from the University of Toronto, who brings a wealth of experience in developing cutting-edge machine-learning solutions. In his previous role, he spearheaded an engineering team within the Canadian National Defence, crafting an AI-powered cybersecurity solution.

* Warm intros to design companies that spend a lot of time making drawings — email us at [mohammed@draftaid.io](mailto:mohammed@draftaid.io).
* Follow us on [**Linkedin.**](https://www.linkedin.com/company/draftaid)

### **The Problem**

Every construction project is slowed down by drawings mistakes:

* Building code violations
* Dimensions that don’t match between structural, architectural, civil, MEP drawings
* Materials mismatch for doors, windows, cabinets etc.
* Ownership/responsibility confusion

These inconsistencies cause rework, schedule delays, and frustrated clients. They happen on **every project**, and can cost **6-7 figures per job**. 

Humans aren’t the best to check hundreds or thousands of pages.

An AI agent analyzes all project documents, architectural / structural / civil / MEP drawings, project specifications, and building codes, and flag issues like dimension mismatches, materials mismatches, ownership/responsibility confusion, missing info, ADA/code red flags, and uncoordinated addenda.

No workflow change. No training. Just fewer errors and better margins.

We’re already running our agent on Tenant Improvement, K-12, civic, industrial, healthcare, affordable housing, and residential projects.

Hi!

We’re [Jesse](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jc10/) and [Gautham](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gautham-ramachandran-74b5712a4/), and we’re building [Bidflow](https://usebidflow.com/) to help electricians bid on more jobs. Bidflow is an AI copilot that helps electrician companies sift through tedious documents and automate the repetitive work that goes into quoting a job.

Ask: Do you know any electrical contractors? If so, introduce us at [founders@tryghostship.dev](mailto:founders@tryghostship.dev) or [book a demo with us](https://calendly.com/jessechoe10/demo-with-bidflow).

# The Problem

Electrical estimating - the process of figuring out how much an electrical construction project will cost is super tedious and can take anywhere from a few hours to months. Imagine reading through 500-page PDFs, counting hundreds of small symbols per page on 50 pages of complicated circuits, and manually entering thousands of numbers on slow, legacy software.

Electrical estimators do this process everyday but manually, and most of the time, they lose the job by a small margin. Estimating is the only way electrical contractors make revenue, and they do it manually because one mistake can cost thousands of dollars and they need to be careful!

# Our Solution

Because estimating is such a careful process, electrical contractors still do everything manually, especially because AI is hard to trust. That’s why we built Bidflow - an AI copilot for electrical estimating that serves as an assistant not a replacement.

Bidflow is designed with context to think like an electrician and most importantly, show the estimator “proof of work”, turning the estimators job more into reviewing the AI’s mistakes. We’re able to process all of your project documents and save you time in reading through hundreds of pages of fine print.

Bidflow also has the same features as the legacy softwares these estimators use, but it combines everything together, making it an all-in-one platform that also saves estimators time switching between the softwares.

<https://youtu.be/GzvbzYwVzZM>

### Our Team

We decided to target electrical contractors because we both have family in the industry who’ve complained about how slow work has been. We then decided to go door-to-door in the Bay Area and got our first design partner.

Jesse (CEO, right) - **Top 1%** competitive coder in the US; **Jane Street** extern. Gautham (CTO, left) - Bootstrapped to **$120K** at **16**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=96918&key=user_uploads/1512811/3c223688-5b55-49b7-b1bf-e08439b4b1e4)

### Why Now?

Construction is picking up in the United States, and the demand for electrical work is going up due to the data center boom. New data centers are being built left and right, meaning there’s a lot of electrical construction projects in the market. A huge boost in estimating efficiency would give the faster electrical contractors a huge advantage in winning jobs, and with AI agents getting better now more than ever, now is the time to bring AI into the electrical estimating workforce.

launches.body:
**002C:** “002A, 5.3 mm left.”

**002B:** “002A, you’re running low. Next pallet is on the way.”

**002C:** “Am I clear to come in?”

**002A:** “Aligned. Panel released. You’re clear.”

**002C:** “Fastening.”

**002B:** “Next load arriving now.”

This isn’t a human crew talking.

**It’s three robots building a solar farm together.**

**TL;DR: Libra Robotics is building robotic crews for utility-scale solar. Most robots automate a task; Libra automates the installation workflow. Our specialized robots work together to transport modules, pick and place them, align them with millimeter-level precision, fasten them, and inspect the result.**

We believe the right unit of automation for solar isn’t a single robot - it’s the crew. Utility-scale solar module installation is highly repetitive but deeply interconnected: every module has to be staged, transported, picked, positioned, aligned, fastened, and inspected, repeated across millions of modules on a single project. Automating only one of those steps still leaves people and equipment coordinating everything around it.

So we built a robotic crew. LIBRA-002A picks, aligns, and places modules; LIBRA-002B autonomously stages and transports them; and LIBRA-002C follows behind to fasten them. The robots communicate continuously, share task state, coordinate handoffs, and assist one another to keep the installation workflow moving as one system.

In just 10 weeks, Libra has secured **20+ MW of planned deployments**, **7+ GW of customer LOIs (\~$56M in potential deployment value)**, and is **fully booked for pilots through March 2027**. Demand already exceeds the capacity of our current robot fleet, so we’re building more robots for upcoming deployments.

**▶ Watch how it works:** <https://youtu.be/GGWhvq3RGRU>

# 

### **Why Solar**

Utility-scale solar is one of the clearest places to start.

Contractors already face persistent labor shortages, just as electricity demand is accelerating from data centers, AI infrastructure, and new industrial loads. Global **data center electricity demand** alone is expected to nearly double by 2030, adding roughly **465 TWh of annual demand**. Nearly half of that growth is expected to be met by renewable energy, with solar playing a major role.

A single project can stretch across hundreds of acres and require crews to install millions of modules, often in remote environments and 100°F+ heat.

But installing a solar module isn’t one task. It’s a sequence: **stage → transport → pick → place → align → fasten → inspect.** Each step depends on the one before it.

That makes solar particularly well suited for a coordinated robotic crew.

### **Why a Crew**

Most construction robots automate a single task. But solar farms are built by crews because the work itself is interconnected: if transportation falls behind, installation stops; if placement is inaccurate, fastening stops; and if one machine operates faster than the rest of the workflow, it simply creates another bottleneck.

**Our approach is to optimize the crew, not just the individual robot.** Specialized robots can coordinate around the workflow, rebalance work when one part falls behind, and scale throughput by adding additional robots where they are needed.

This also avoids trying to build one giant machine that does everything. Each robot can remain relatively specialized while the capabilities of the crew expand over time.

### **What We Built**

**We built a coordinated robotic system for utility-scale solar installation.** LIBRA-002A picks modules from the staging area, positions them on the structure, and performs millimeter-level alignment. LIBRA-002B autonomously transports and stages modules to keep installation moving. LIBRA-002C follows behind to fasten each module in place.

The robots operate as one system. They continuously share task state, coordinate handoffs, and communicate when each step is complete. The system knows when a module is arriving, when placement and alignment are finished, and when the fastening robot is clear to move in.

The architecture is designed to scale with the jobsite. More transportation, installation, or fastening robots can be added as throughput requirements increase, while new capabilities can be introduced without redesigning the entire system. Over time, this also enables 24/7 continuous operation, with robotic crews keeping material and installation work moving through the night.

We deliver the system through **Robot-as-a-Service**. Libra provides the robotic crew, deployment, supervision, and maintenance. Contractors don’t purchase robots or take on upfront robotics CapEx - they simply pay for the work performed.

## 

### **Where We Are**

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We are building a new kind of camera that can see through walls using radio waves. We provide construction, industrial inspection, and security teams with an accurate map of hidden objects behind walls and composite surfaces.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iEHRvcKN8g>

## **The Problem**

Most of the built world is opaque.

Pipes, cables, and structural elements hide behind walls until they're discovered mid-project, driving $20B+ a year in avoidable rework.

Defects remain hidden inside composites until parts break.

Entry teams are missing critical information before they breach a barrier.

## **The Solution**

An imaging platform that uses radio waves to see behind walls. It works just like a camera, requiring no training and producing high-resolution images that are instantly understandable. The resulting point cloud is natively to scale, accurate down to 1mm.

## **The Team**

Four engineers who've worked together for 8+ years, shipped multiple zero-to-one hardware products, and hold 250+ patents.

**Bilgehan** — PhD in electromagnetics; led antenna technologies on four iPhone generations, shipping the first phones with UWB and 5G mmWave; inventor of the zirconia dielectric resonator antenna.

**Brian** — built the earliest iPhone prototypes at Apple, co-invented iPhone multitouch and the Nest Learning Thermostat; degrees in Electrical and Civil Engineering.

**George** — MIT physicist; built x-ray imagers, retinal implants, optical sensors and the world's smallest laser projector.

**Paul** — Berkeley Mech.E.; ex-Apple and Humane product design lead; co-invented iPhone haptic Touch ID, IPX8 sealing.

## **What we built**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108275&key=user_uploads/2724984/c00b3438-c7f7-433f-941d-e021791e51c5)

We've built the hardware and imaging algorithms that can see behind composite layers and common building materials (sheetrock, tiles, marble, quartz, brick and insulation). Next step is our handheld platform that fuses our radio imaging with RGB and thermal cameras.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108275&key=user_uploads/2724984/f1cf1ffa-8b23-4780-b363-13b0db90832d)

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: Alloovium automates compliance for major construction projects 🚧** Construction is 13% of global GDP, and it runs on paperwork. Nobody in the industry wants another platform — they want what they already have brought together in one place. Alloovium is that unifying layer: it reads everything the project produces from the tools you already use, and turns it into cited answers you can trust and the documentation that moves the job forward — compliant with the builder's own management system, every answer cited to its source sentence, a human sign-off on anything AI-drafted.

[**https://youtu.be/wVPJL3o8PzM**](https://youtu.be/wVPJL3o8PzM)

**🚧 The problem**

On major projects, the record keeps losing: 80% of megaprojects blow their budget or schedule, and sums in dispute average a third of contract budgets. We think the root cause is hiding in plain sight — in the paperwork.

**The root cause:** paperwork is a state in time — every document a snapshot of a project thats moving daily. The documents aren't a pile, they're a web: the safety plan leans on procedures; procedures lean on templates, registers and licences; and the tender made promises all of them have to keep true. Across every company delivering the job. People spend their days dragging the paper back to reality instead of moving the job forward.

**The consequence:** one change means five documents to amend, and nobody catches the missed one until an auditor, regulator or client's lawyer does. In some jurisdictions: up to 25 years jail for directors and a $20M fine for the GC.

**The cost of coping:** engineers who trained for years to build spend their days chasing paper instead. One tier-1 team is spending $2.5M and 40–50 people on a single 400-page submission of management plans — and that's before the project even starts.

**The unlock:** a sleepless project sentinel, keeping watch on the documented rules, unlocking the experts to focus on the build.

**🔨 What Alloovium does**

* **Documents, Apps, Correspondence and Conversations centralised in the Project.** A singular place where the project becomes a reality.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105028&key=user_uploads/3047254/69afa2af-4a4e-4376-ad5e-186084b42ee4)

* **Cited answers over every project document.** Click the citation, land on the exact source sentence.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105028&key=user_uploads/3047254/6687ff2d-1620-404b-b4a9-a6f8a8fd5aae)

* **Routines.** Build repeatable workflows that are triggered by on-site events to always stay ahead of the game on your paperwork.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105028&key=user_uploads/3047254/ec46815c-e232-43eb-a583-ec74c80f25ff)

* **Drafting from the project itself.** Call transcript to a formatted and actionable document in minutes, with AI-authorship tracking, a human still refines and reviews it.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105028&key=user_uploads/3047254/503df904-c919-46e3-9e31-c3e2c768db67)

* **Continual compliance sweeps** against the builder's own IMS, clause by clause. Our new engine's first end-to-end sweep landed **39 cited findings** on one project.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105028&key=user_uploads/3047254/fd973fc4-a947-4f2a-8e9c-d2e42671b97f)

* Plus meeting/inbox capture, voice to text data capture, licence-expiry alerts, and live SharePoint + Procore sync.

**📈 Traction**

Deploying across $400M in active projects, including a subsidiary of BMD (one of Australia's largest privately owned civil contractors). ISO compliance product in beta with a 30-year auditor as design partner.

**👋 Who we are**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105028&key=user_uploads/3047254/aba0a4bb-7496-4a42-960f-bb96be1c8307)

* [**Zander Schweitzer**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3047254) grew up in construction, spent his fifth birthday in the back of a bulldozer, drove dump trucks, and worked as a site engineer before quitting to start this.
* [@Cielo Nicolosi](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3650351) has coded since he was 8, was founding engineer at four startups, placed top 0.25% of his state, and won Australia's largest student hackathon.
* Around us: an exited construction-tech founder, an ex-LexisNexis Senior Data Scientist, and a founding SDR from Askable.

**The Problem:**

Meet Jeremy. He’s a project manager at a mid-sized contractor, and his job is to secure projects and then make sure the company doesn’t lose money on already thin margins.

A bid invite lands in his inbox. To put together one number his firm can send in, Jeremy has to read thousands of pages. A 400-page project manual, drawings, insurance, spec sections, and so much more. Buried somewhere inside all this print is a line that can ultimately decide whether this job makes or loses money. From a liquidated-damages clause to a scope item sneakily handed to the mechanical contractor, if Jeremy misses it, it’s a $5K-$10K mistake.

Jeremy’s got one week, three other bids on his desk, and no way to read all of it as carefully as he’d like. So he reads what he can and sends in a number.

Say he wins. A change in the signed contract by the General Contractor or a sneaky difference in vendor pricing costs the company thousands after the fact. Every step of the way requires hundreds of pages of reading and referencing done under a deadline. And Jeremy does this for every job.

**The Solution:**\
FlowManual automates these historical workflows that contractors run on, allowing teams to submit bids and complete projects faster than ever before. Here’s a couple major features:

* AI Takeoffs from drawings
* Drawing comparisons / overlay
* Bid leveling
* Contract Review

Our software doesn’t do the job for you, but it works alongside you to reduce time spent and mistakes made.

**About Us:**\
Michael and David were college roommates and engineers at Harvard. When renovations for a heater in our dorm took 6 weeks, we poked at the problem, realizing it stems from a larger issue. Through hundreds of conversations with professionals, we found an industry that ran on file cabinets, Excel, and page-by-page manual review.\

launches.tagline: Robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars. We’re proving the technology by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth — utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re [James](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesemerick/) and [Lewis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewis-c-jones/) - co-founders of [Cosmic Robotics](https://www.cosmicrobotics.com). 

**TL;DR**

**We build robotic construction equipment to build a city on Mars**. We’re proving the technology today by building large-scale infrastructure on Earth – utility-scale solar farms and hyperscale data centers. Our first machine, Cosmic-1, has already installed tens of thousands of solar panels in the field and more than doubled the productivity of traditional crews.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Dl00xlJbcI> 

**❌ The problem**

After working at NASA JPL, SpaceX, and Relativity Space, we believe rockets are no longer the limiting factor to space exploration and that the first humans will land on Mars by 2034. **The new bottleneck is construction**. We won't be sending thousands of construction workers to Mars to build the energy, compute, and housing needed to sustain even a small city. **It has to be built by robots that don't exist yet**.

On Earth we have a similar problem - **we’ve lost the ability to build**. Construction productivity has declined for 50 years while manufacturing and agriculture became 10-15x more productive through automation. **The missing technology is robotic manipulation for the tasks still done by hand**: lifting, placing, fastening.

Meanwhile, there is a generational infrastructure buildout happening right now. **$7 trillion** is going into AI data centers, power, and compute over the next six years, **more than the Apollo Program, Manhattan Project, and Interstate Highway System combined**. 40% of US data center projects are running behind schedule, and the skilled labor shortage is the #1 cause. 

**🤖 What we've built**

Cosmic-1 is a 10,000 lb autonomous robot capable of heavy-lift manipulation. In solar, it picks up 90 lb panels and places them onto racking with millimeter precision in any environment: 100-degree heat, freezing rain, snow, and dust. It seamlessly integrates into existing construction processes. Across tens of thousands of cycles it has more than doubled the labor productivity of solar installation, on some of the largest solar projects in the US.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/bb5f86ec-a23b-4ffd-a173-87f36ce6fb1c)

**👬 The Team**

We come at this problem from two angles. James (CEO) grew up on construction sites, then spent his career bringing robots to the field with Built Robotics and Autodesk Research. He learned you don't change the oldest industry in the world by disrupting it; you earn your way in by giving crews better tools.

Lewis' (CTO) life ambition is to build a city on Mars. His work at NASA, SpaceX, and Relativity Space spans rocket engines, launch vehicles, satellites, space stations, and, yes, Martian robots. When it became clear the space industry was well on its way to Mars, he went looking for the construction robots. When he didn't find them, we started Cosmic.

We’ve brought together a team of industry experts with experience building robots, rockets, drones, self-driving cars, humanoids, and nuclear reactor operations. We know what it takes to get a machine to show up day-in-day-out on the jobsite.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106899&key=user_uploads/522502/87f30a8e-6f83-490e-8bef-04225d1a525e)

**🚀 What's next**

We're scaling in solar, taking Cosmic-1 into data center construction, and working with NASA on lunar construction robotics. Revenue and data from deployments on Earth train the systems we'll deploy on Mars.

**🙏 Our asks**

1. **Know a hyperscaler or neocloud construction team?** Please connect us.
2. **Share this post** and [follow our journey](https://www.linkedin.com/company/cosmic-robotics/).

👉 Contact us at [james@cosmicrobotics.com](mailto:james@cosmicrobotics.com) | [cosmicrobotics.com](http://cosmicrobotics.com)

launches.tagline: Autonomous rovers building the 'Google Maps' of subsurface infrastructure
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/5IY3vHEJ7J4>

Construction has a mapping problem. Of the $2.2T in annual US construction spending, $150B is wasted due to a lack of subsurface knowledge. All construction starts from the ground up, and more often than not, unexpected assets underneath the surface will hold a construction project back. Whether it's an unknown utility line, unexpected rock layer, or old foundation that wasn’t on any design map, the costs of delays from underground conflicts quickly add up. 

Take utility strikes, when an excavator hits an active utility line. For every dollar spent on the explicit repair cost of that utility line itself, the contractor loses an additional $30 per repair-dollar in project delays, insurance claims, idle work crews, and increased insurance premiums. For a hyperscale project such as data center construction, a single day of delay can cost the cloud-provider up to $14 million dollars for that single day.

In metropolitan areas, maps are incomplete at best and none create a unified picture of critical infrastructure, making excavation especially dangerous when natural gas or electric lines are broken.

Enter SubVysion. We’ve built a fleet of autonomous rovers carrying ground-penetrating radar and other sensors that create a centimeter-accurate map of subsurface infrastructure. Our hardware is the first and the best to map the entirety of US infrastructure. Using our rovers, we comprehensively map construction sites, city streets, and even larger indoor buildings, at 100x better granularity and 10x the speed (with a single rover) compared to our competitors. We process vast amounts of data using machine learning and agents, and output that data into an easy-to-understand 3D scene. 

Who are we? Maxwell Stone was an early ML engineer at Roboflow (YC S20), and Wenson Tang built the world’s smallest and cheapest LiDAR-capable drone for adverse environments. We both studied computer science at the University of Pennsylvania. Together, we’re building SubVysion to map the entirety of America’s subsurface infrastructure.

We’re currently on job sites in Philadelphia and Texas, helping our first market of utility contractors save hundreds of thousands of dollars every year. We’re soon to expand our mapping services to municipalities and energy providers as we scale up our rover fleet and capacity!

If you’re in the energy, infrastructure, or hyperscale construction world, we’d love to hear from you at [founders@subvysion.com](mailto:founders@subvysion.com)!
